proposals.evidence: The kāṭ-/kaṭ- verb belongs to Turner kartati cuts. Platts s.v. kāṭnā independently attests biting as an ordinary sense of the same verb. These are unaccompanied inflected forms, or an imperative/past pair of that verb; no take/give/eat auxiliary is present.

proposals.evidence: Turner khādati includes the original chew/bite senses and regional khā- eat; the same article explicitly lists analogical khādh- past forms. These single-verb biting responses are linked to that verbal family, with local past/imperative morphology retained.
